scenes.text: The 1960s marshmallow test measured kids’ ability to wait.
Kids who waited tended to achieve better academic results later.
Long‑term follow‑up found patient people earned more as adults.
Patient participants often earned noticeably more over their careers.
But the effect isn’t magic; it reflects self‑control habits.
Self‑control can be trained like a muscle.
Three steps to build it: set tiny goals, delay small rewards, track progress.
Now you know why a simple marshmallow matters more than you think:
